analysis.title: Anatomy Of Higher Volatility Hints At More Trouble
key_insights: Volatility across markets is setting a higher floor even as underlying assets correct, which raises the potential for the next equity drawdown to be more violent than the last.

10Y Treasury yield has retreated more than 40bp from early October highs and settled around 5% after hotter-than-forecast CPI. Brent has fallen more than $20/bbl from last month's highs. Both remain well above their June lows.
VIX appears to be finding support around 20 this week, reversing the downtrend that took it to about 14 in August. MOVE has stayed around 90, roughly the 85th percentile of its one-year range.

Speculative exposure in oil and Treasuries is near year-to-date lows and momentum indicators are oversold. The author says positioning exhaustion should not be confused with a fundamental repricing, and that persistent elevated vol after large directional unwinds means markets price uncertainty beyond the positioning cycle.

The five-sigma equity drawdown after the midterm election delivered a shock comparable to the April 2025 tariff turmoil, but against higher inflation. The Fed's policy flexibility that helped contain earlier equity declines cannot be relied on.
Waller and Logan have turned more hawkish. October headline inflation is estimated to have risen more than 4% from a year earlier.

With the midterms over, the Trump administration may have less incentive to counter equity weakness with market-friendly policy. This challenges both the Fed put and the Trump put, and 'dip alpha' from buying dips may be harder to capture as selloffs persist.
A z-score composite of Brent ATM vol, VIX and MOVE, calibrated by a realized vol factor, trends upward and is approaching April 2025 levels.
MOVE had 32 consecutive sessions above 90, ending Nov. 9, the fifth-longest streak since 2020. MOVE has led the rise in cross-asset vol.
The usual year-end compression of equity vol looks vulnerable. VIX is diverging from its seasonal path, which may mean conventional vol-selling strategies face a different regime.

The Realized Volatility Index (delta-hedged short-dated S&P 500 straddles) is on course for its largest week-over-week gain this year, challenging a downtrend that has lasted all year. Realized vol is becoming more consequential relative to the cost of optionality, a possible shift away from a regime that rewarded short-vol strategies.

tension_points.bull_case: Speculative exposure in oil and Treasuries is near year-to-date lows and momentum is oversold, which could support tactical stabilization.
tension_points.bear_case: Positioning exhaustion is not a fundamental repricing. Elevated vol persists despite large unwinds, the Fed and Trump puts are weaker, and the next shock could be more violent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A return of VIX toward its August low near 14 and of MOVE below 90 would undercut the higher-floor thesis. The report does not state this explicitly.
